If someone believes they deserve something because they worked hard, they might struggle with setbacks or failures, seeing them as undeserved rather than learning opportunities. This could affect their overall approach to challenges and their ability to adapt. I also think about the difference between deserving and being entitled. Deserving implies that one has earned something through effort, while being entitled might suggest a sense of ownership or expectation without necessarily earning it. So, in this case, if someone worked hard, they might feel they deserve the better seats, but does that mean they're entitled to a fun time? It's a bit of a stretch because fun is a personal experience that can't be guaranteed by effort alone. Furthermore, there's the question of whether deserving something leads to happiness. Even if someone works hard and achieves their goal, they might not feel happy or fulfilled if other aspects of their life are lacking. So, while they might deserve the better seats, their overall sense of deserving a fun time might depend on more than just their effort at the concert. I also consider the role of luck. Sometimes, despite working hard, things don't go as planned, and other times, people might achieve their goals without much effort. So, does deserving something always align with the outcome? It seems like there's an element of chance involved, which complicates the idea of what one deserves based solely on effort. In summary, while working hard to get better concert seats might make someone feel they deserve a fun time, there are several factors to consider.
